name: Health & Medicine
summary: AI is routine in radiology and clinical note-taking, chatbots field health questions at vast scale, AI-designed drugs reach late-stage trials, and regulators loosen some rules while tightening others.

regions.name: Imaging & diagnostics
regions.summary: Radiology makes up about three quarters of the AI devices on the FDA's list. A large randomized trial and a German rollout study show AI-supported breast screening detects more cancers.

landmarks.name: MASAI trial interval cancer results in The Lancet
landmarks.summary: Swedish randomized trial of 105,934 women: AI-supported screening had a non-inferior interval cancer rate (1.55 vs 1.76 per 1,000) and higher sensitivity than double reading.

landmarks.name: FDA AI device list passes 1,600
landmarks.summary: The FDA's list, updated in September 2026, holds about 1,610 AI-enabled devices authorized through June 2026. About 76% (1,230) sit in the radiology panel.
landmarks.note: Counts tallied from the FDA table; the page states no total.

landmarks.name: PRAIM: AI in German breast screening
landmarks.summary: Real-world study of 463,094 women at 12 German screening sites: cancer detection was 17.6% higher with AI-supported reading (6.7 vs 5.7 per 1,000), with no rise in recalls.

regions.whyItMatters: Imaging is where medical AI has the most approvals and the strongest trial evidence, so it shows what real clinical adoption looks like.
regions.openQuestion: Does finding more cancers with AI mean fewer deaths, and do the results hold outside European double-reading programs?

deepDives.title: List of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices (FDA)
deepDives.why: The primary record of authorized AI devices, with panel, company and decision date.

deepDives.title: AI improves breast cancer screening: expert reactions (SMC Spain)
deepDives.why: Independent researchers on what the MASAI trial does and does not show.

deepDives.title: PRAIM study dataset (Dryad)
deepDives.why: Open data behind the German AI mammography implementation study.

deepDives.title: NEJM AI
deepDives.why: Journal dedicated to clinical evaluations of AI.

regions.name: Clinical documentation & scribes
regions.summary: Ambient AI scribes that draft visit notes have spread fast across US health systems. A multisite study found modest time savings, and Epic's built-in scribe now competes with Microsoft and Abridge.

landmarks.name: JAMA multisite study of AI scribes
landmarks.summary: Study of 8,581 ambulatory clinicians at five US academic systems tied AI scribes to 16 fewer documentation minutes per 8 patient hours; after-hours time was unchanged.

landmarks.name: Dragon Copilot passes 100,000 clinicians
landmarks.summary: At HIMSS 2026 Microsoft said more than 100,000 clinicians rely on Dragon Copilot in daily practice and offered partner-built AI apps and agents through its marketplace.

landmarks.name: Two thirds of Epic hospitals use ambient AI
landmarks.summary: AJMC study of 2,784 Epic hospitals found 62.6% had adopted ambient AI by June 2025; DAX Copilot, Abridge and ThinkAndor made up over 80% of implementations.

landmarks.name: Epic releases its own AI Charting
landmarks.summary: Epic released AI Charting, a built-in feature that listens during visits, drafts the note and queues up orders, putting the largest US records vendor up against scribe makers.

regions.whyItMatters: Scribes are among the most widely adopted generative AI tools in medicine and an early test of whether AI eases clinician workload in practice.
regions.openQuestion: Do scribes reduce burnout and cost, or mainly raise visit volume and billing, and how accurate are the notes?

deepDives.title: Ambient AI Tool Adoption in US Hospitals and Associated Factors (AJMC)
deepDives.why: Peer-reviewed snapshot of which hospitals adopted ambient AI and which vendors lead.

deepDives.title: AI scribes deliver modest time savings, but still boost clinician experience
deepDives.why: Explainer on the JAMA study, with the authors on what the time savings mean.

deepDives.title: Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare Delivery Systems (PHTI)
deepDives.why: Independent institute's report on early uses of AI in health systems, including ambient scribes.

deepDives.title: AI Index 2026: Medicine chapter (Stanford HAI)
deepDives.why: Yearly data review; covers clinical note generation, device approvals and diagnosis studies.

regions.name: Drug development & trials
regions.summary: An AI-discovered drug has entered Phase III, large funding rounds continue, and US and EU regulators have published shared principles for AI use across the medicines lifecycle.

landmarks.name: Insilico starts Phase III for rentosertib
landmarks.summary: Insilico began a 52-week, placebo-controlled Phase III trial of rentosertib, its AI-discovered TNIK inhibitor for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, planned for 320 patients in China.

landmarks.name: Isomorphic Labs raises $2.1B
landmarks.summary: Alphabet's AI drug design company raised a $2.1B Series B led by Thrive Capital, with Alphabet, GV, MGX, Temasek, CapitalG and the UK Sovereign AI Fund also investing.

landmarks.name: FDA and EMA joint AI principles
landmarks.summary: The two regulators set out ten guiding principles for good AI practice in the medicines lifecycle, from early research and clinical trials to manufacturing and safety monitoring.

regions.whyItMatters: Drug discovery is the highest-stakes test of whether AI can speed up science, and no AI-discovered drug has yet been approved.
regions.openQuestion: Will AI-designed drugs succeed in late-stage trials at a higher rate than conventionally discovered ones?

deepDives.title: Guiding principles of good AI practice in drug development
deepDives.why: The ten joint EMA and FDA principles in full, in a short primary document.

deepDives.title: Artificial Intelligence for Drug Development (FDA CDER)
deepDives.why: The FDA's running hub for guidance and policy on AI in drug and biologic development.

deepDives.title: 2025 AI Observatory report (EMA)
deepDives.why: European regulator's yearly review of how AI is used in medicines regulation.

deepDives.title: A generative AI-discovered TNIK inhibitor for IPF: a randomized phase 2a trial
deepDives.why: Peer-reviewed Phase IIa results for rentosertib in Nature Medicine, the basis for Phase III.

regions.name: Patient-facing assistants & mental health
regions.summary: Hundreds of millions ask chatbots health questions weekly. Products now connect to medical records, while US states restrict AI therapy and companion bots after safety concerns.

landmarks.name: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Health
landmarks.summary: A dedicated ChatGPT space that links medical records and wellness apps; OpenAI says more than 230M people ask health and wellness questions on ChatGPT each week.

landmarks.name: California SB 243 on companion chatbots
landmarks.summary: State law requiring companion chatbot operators to disclose that users are talking to AI and to keep protocols for suicide and self-harm, effective January 2026.

landmarks.name: Illinois bans AI therapy
landmarks.summary: Illinois law bars using AI to provide therapy or make therapeutic decisions, while allowing administrative support for licensed professionals. Nevada passed a similar limit.

landmarks.name: First trial of a generative AI therapy chatbot
landmarks.summary: Dartmouth's randomized trial of Therabot in 106 people, published in NEJM AI, reported a 51% average drop in depression symptoms and a 31% drop in anxiety symptoms.

regions.whyItMatters: This is where most people actually meet medical AI, largely outside clinical oversight and medical device rules.
regions.openQuestion: Do health chatbots improve outcomes for ordinary users, and who is liable when their advice causes harm?

deepDives.title: Health advisory: generative AI chatbots and wellness apps for mental health (APA)
deepDives.why: American Psychological Association's evidence review and recommendations on chatbot use.

deepDives.title: KFF Health Misinformation Tracking Poll: AI and Health Information
deepDives.why: 2024 US survey on how often people use chatbots for health advice and how far they trust it.

deepDives.title: HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health
deepDives.why: OpenAI benchmark of 5,000 health conversations graded against physician-written rubrics.

deepDives.title: The Batch: Illinois follows Nevada on therapy chatbots
deepDives.why: Short account of the state laws, their fines and the debate over restricting AI therapy.

regions.name: Medical AI regulation & validation
regions.summary: The FDA has relaxed oversight of decision-support software and wearables while still weighing how to handle generative AI devices. The EU has delayed high-risk rules for medical devices to 2028.

landmarks.name: FDA relaxes CDS and wellness guidance
landmarks.summary: Updated final guidances, issued without prior public comment, replace the 2022 clinical decision support and 2019 general wellness policies and widen what counts as non-device.

landmarks.name: FDA panel on generative AI mental health devices
landmarks.summary: FDA's Digital Health Advisory Committee met on evidence and monitoring for generative AI therapy chatbots; the agency had not yet cleared any generative AI mental health tool.

landmarks.name: EU delays AI Act rules for medical devices
landmarks.summary: The AI Omnibus, in force since 27 July 2026, extends the transition for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products, which include medical devices, to 2 August 2028.

regions.whyItMatters: Rules written for fixed software are being stretched to cover generative models, and the outcome decides what reaches patients.
regions.openQuestion: How should regulators evaluate and monitor generative AI whose outputs vary and whose models change after approval?
